claim: MITRE ATT&CK is a knowledge base of attacker behaviour derived from real-world observations.
quote: MITRE ATT&CK is a curated knowledge base and model for cyber adversary behavior ... it proved useful to categorize observed behavior across relevant real-world adversary groups
issue: Body says it directly; the abstract adds "based on real-world observations" (p. iii, PDF p. 2).

claim: ATT&CK was developed by the MITRE Corporation in 2013.
quote: The first ATT&CK model was created in September 2013 and was primarily focused on the Windows enterprise environment.
issue: Created Sept 2013 within MITRE FMX; publicly released May 2015. "developed in 2013" matches the first model, not the public release.

claim: ATT&CK organises behaviour into a hierarchy of tactics, techniques, sub-techniques and procedures.
quote: Tactics, denoting short-term, tactical adversary goals during an attack; • Techniques, describing the means by which adversaries achieve tactical goals; • Sub-techniques, describing more specific means by which adversaries achieve tactical goals at a lower level than techniques; and • Documented adversary usage of techniques, their procedures, and other metadata.
issue: The four levels are Strom's, and sub-techniques sit "at a lower level than techniques". Strom never says "hierarchy", and notes a procedure "can span multiple techniques and sub-techniques" (Sect. 3.4.1, p. 9 printed, PDF p. 19), and a technique can sit under several tactics, so it is not a strict tree. The 2020 revision is the one that holds sub-techniques; the 2018 original did not.
